Hi Ava,

Thanks for the ongoing partnership — we launched the new summarization flow three months ago and we're seeing token consumption grow faster than expected. Our contract with Redwood is up for renewal in August, but we need to implement an uplift mid-contract to avoid throttling our production workload.

Current commit: 1.2M tokens/month. Expected uplift: +650k tokens/month, starting June 1.

Can you send over pricing options that cover:
- A mid-term top-up (prorated) for June–Aug, with the remainder annualized at renewal;
- An option to annualize the new total now (co-term to next Aug 31) and pay a single annual invoice;
- A voucher/installment model where we pay 50% now and 50% at renewal day;

We have procurement constraints: net-30 preferred, one PO, and we typically ask for an early-payment discount if we do annual prepay. Also — can you confirm whether a staged payment would affect our priority support SLA or burst allocation?

I've attached a draft internal forecast and the current renewal worksheet. We can put legal on a DocuSign if we get commercial terms agreed. Need to finalize by May 20 to align invoicing and infra reservation.

Appreciate any options and examples of how you've handled co-terming for similar customers.

Best,
Marta
Head of Platform Engineering
Quantify Inc.

Ben / Karthik — forwarding Quantify's ask. Key facts: +650k tokens/mo uplift, want either prorated top-up or co-term annualization now, procurement prefers net-30 and one PO. Need commercial answer by May 20; want quote by EOD Wed.

Proposed pricing scenarios (high level):
1) Prorated top-up (June–Aug) then annual renewal for full amount on Aug 31:
   - Top-up priced at list with 10% staged-payment discount if they pay the top-up invoice within 30 days;
   - No SLA change; burst buffer stays the same but priority allocation during capacity contention is tied to committed capacity (i.e., uplift counts once invoiced/committed).
2) Immediate annualize (co-term now to Aug 31):
   - Annualize new qty (1.85M tokens/month) at a 7% volume discount across the full year;
   - Offer Net-30, or Net-45 with a 2% additional discount for prepay scenario;
   - Prioritized capacity and extended SLAs are available on the Dedicated tier (requires paperwork).
3) Voucher / split payment (50/50):
   - 50% now on a pro-rated invoice, 50% at renewal. Offer a $25k onboarding/implementation credit if they sign a 12-month commitment for the new total.

Notes:
- If we want to be aggressive, we can bump scenario (1) staged discount to 12% but require Net-30 + PO within 7 days of quote;
- Finance: need to confirm revenue recognition for voucher split (Karthik) and whether we can allow net-45 and still hit ARR targets for the quarter.

I've attached an internal spreadsheet with per-option TCV math and discount impact. Ask: Ben, approve final discount band and whether $25k onboarding credit is acceptable. Karthik, confirm if split payment creates any finance/recognition issues.

Thanks,
Ava

- Lead with option (1) prorated top-up but be willing to convert to (2) annualize at quoting time. Offer 10% on the top-up invoice (as you proposed) — that is within comp and shouldn't set a bad precedent.
- If they push to annualize now, increase to 12% discount on the total annualized TCV but require Net-30 + signed PO within 10 business days.
- Approve the $25k onboarding credit, but make it contingent on a 12-month commitment to the new total and one annual invoice at renewal.

Karthik — please confirm quickly that a 50/50 voucher split would be recognized in a compliant way; if finance prefers, we can require full invoicing within the quarter and move the second payment to be a renewal invoice.

Ava — once Karthik signs off, send the formal quote (include both top-up invoice and a single-line annualize option) and include the DocuSign link. Mention the onboarding credit as a line item credit. Add the HubSpot deal HS-892134 and send me a copy before you hit send.
